sources.entry: macUSB - A bootable macOS / OS X installer creator for Apple Silicon Macs. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Kruszoneq/macUSB) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: macUSB is a free macOS app that creates bootable USB media for macOS, OS X, Linux, and Windows from local files or a built-in macOS installer downloader.
summary.what_it_does: macUSB is a guided macOS app for making bootable USB drives or SD cards on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. It can use local .dmg, .cdr, .iso, and .app sources for macOS, or fetch macOS installers directly from Apple through a built-in downloader that can also show Public Beta releases and save installers as .app or read-only .dmg. It supports Linux and Windows .iso images, with optional Windows setup automation via Autounattend.xml for Windows 10 and 11. It also includes a raw .iso/.img writer that verifies written data with SHA-256, and a checksum tool for supported images. The README lists support for macOS families from Golden Gate 27 back to Tiger 10.4, with per-version limits noted.
use_cases: make a bootable macOS installer USB on a Mac
download a macOS installer from Apple and prepare it for USB
create a Windows install USB from an ISO on a Mac
create a Linux live USB from an ISO on a Mac
write a raw ISO or IMG to a USB drive
verify an installer image with SHA-256
how_to_run: Or download the latest release from GitHub Releases
Grant Full Disk Access and Background App Activity to macUSB in System Settings
Open macUSB, choose a local source or use the built-in Downloader
Select the target USB drive or SD card and start the process
For Windows split installs, optionally run: brew install wimlib
stack: Swift (inferred from macOS app; not named in README)
notable: Built-in downloader fetches macOS and older OS X installers directly from Apple servers and detects installers already in /Applications
Supports Linux and Windows ISOs as well as macOS, with automatic distro and architecture detection for 19 tested Linux distributions
Splits Windows install.wim files over FAT32's 4 GB limit into .swm parts using wimlib
Hold Option while selecting a target to reuse existing HFS+ volumes on GPT drives without repartitioning
Available in 15 interface languages, following the system language by default
caveats: Requires macOS Sonoma 14.6 or later on the host Mac
Needs Full Disk Access and Background App Activity permissions to work
Writing a raw image does not guarantee the result is bootable
Some old systems have limits, such as only Sierra 10.12.6 and Tiger multi-DVD needing manual detection; Windows XP and Server 2003 are recognized but cannot be used for media creation
Creating bootable media erases all data on the selected drive
